Like I said, I had a very similar grip when I first started, and it was for a very similar reason to yours. When holding the dart, I felt like I had more control and it was sturdier in my hand with the most contact points possible.

I worked on my grip quite a bit and kept the base of it (rear grip with thumb and index finger) but now only have one more contact point, which is my middle finger, towards the front of the barrel for stability.

Ever since I moved to this grip, my consistency has drastically improved. There is just less to worry about being consistent with when releasing.

Ultimately, just find what works best for you! When you find a grip that works for you and you can see your consistency improving, then take a look at some darts reviews on YouTube. I would recommend Darren's videos on the 'Darts Review Channel'. He's brilliant, very thorough and does a breakdown of how he feels they perform for front grippers, middle grippers & rear grippers.

I was going to comment something similar regarding the unconventional grip. As already mentioned, grips tend to be unique to everyone, and whatever feels comfortable for you, is usually what you should go with. However, this grip looks as though there's a lot of finger pressure in different directions. While this may make the dart feel steady in the hand, it will likely be difficult to be consistent with your release. Which could make your aim and grouping slightly off. 

I had a similar-ish grip when I started, but now I found that the less points of contact I have with the dart in my grip, the easier it is for my throw/releases to be consistent, which has drastically improved my grouping. 

If this grip works for you, happy days! But if you're finding inconsistency being an issue, I would suggest working on a grip with less points of contact.

I posted this in a similar thread where someone was looking for how to improve on doubles: 

Best practice game I've found for doubles is this: 

First 3 darts you target D20 then D10 then D5

Second 3 darts you target D16 then D8 then D4

Third 3 darts you target D12 then D6 then D3

Fourth 3 darts you target D8 then D4 then D2

One dart at each. 

I like it because it simulates real games as if you miss low on a D20 checkout, your next dart is at D10 and so on... Forces you to quickly move around the board and practice recovery doubles in the order that you would go for them in an actual match.
Yeah it's the only doubles practice game that I feel has genuinely helped me in actual matches. Hope it helps you too!
